To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intestinal bacteria are essential for the normal growth and development of the mammalian gut.

intestinal bacteria play a key role in the development of gut-associated lymphoid tissue (the body's primary immune defence in the gut), and that they are involved in the maturation and differentiation of the intestinal epithelial cell lineage, which is a prerequisite for normal intestinal function.
intestinal microbes are important in the regulation of host metabolism and the development of the immune system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by intestinal bacteria in the development of the gut and their influence on the immune system.
the role of intestinal microbiota and their interactions with their eukaryote hosts.
understanding the molecular and cellular basis of these interactions and their impact on health and disease of the host.

gut microbes are a vital component of our body and are indispensable in maintaining the health and well being of their host.
the gut microbiota are not just a passive bystander but are an essential part of the host's physiology.
gut bacteria are not just passengers but are active participants and partners in the host's health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut flora is a complex ecosystem that is a dynamic and interactive system that has evolved to provide a symbiotic relationship between the host and the gut flora.
the gut flora are not just a collection of bacteria but a community with specific functions and that these functions can be manipulated to the benefit of the host.
the gut microbiota is a dynamic ecosystem, which is constantly evolving and interacting with its host in a complex manner.

the gut is a complex and highly organized ecosystem and the bacteria in it have a profound effect on their host.
the gut flora are not just a collection of bacteria that happen to reside in the human intestine, but rather are an integral part of the host and are essential to the health of the host.
